beats.label: S1 · Kate becomes Batwoman
beats.text: Three years after Batman vanished, Kate Kane comes home to save her father from Alice's Wonderland Gang, discovers cousin Bruce is Batman, and dons the suit.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the whole premise: who Batwoman is, why she has the suit, and the sister-versus-father conflict that drives everything after.

beats.label: S1 · Alice is Beth
beats.text: Kate becomes convinced Alice is her twin Beth, presumed dead since childhood; DNA and Alice's own hints confirm it, dividing her from her disbelieving father Jacob.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The identity reveal is the season's engine — every family decision after this hinges on Kate refusing to give up on her sister.

beats.label: S1 · The deer skull
beats.text: Stepmother Catherine confesses she faked Beth's remains with a deer skull to end the search, and Jacob finally accepts that Alice is the daughter he buried.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Aligns Jacob with Kate on Alice's identity and gives Alice a specific reason to punish Catherine — sets up the mid-season murder.

beats.label: S1 · Catherine dies, Jacob framed
beats.text: Alice poisons Catherine at a gala and frames Jacob for the murder, sending him to prison and shattering Mary, who blames Kate for still believing in her sister.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Jacob from the board, breaks the family, and hardens Kate's stance — the emotional pivot the rest of the season plays out from.

beats.label: S1 · Two Beths
beats.text: The Crisis strands a doppelgänger Beth from another Earth in Gotham; the twins cannot both live, and August Cartwright — Mouse's father — snipes Beth thinking she is Alice.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains why the sweet 'Beth' Kate briefly gets back is gone by season's end and why Kate's grief turns to violence next beat.

beats.label: S1 · Kate kills August
beats.text: Enraged by what August did to her mother and sister, Kate strangles him to death; the killing haunts her and confirms Alice cannot be redeemed.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First time Kate crosses the line — the guilt from this defines her final arc and the mindset she carries into her final trip.

beats.label: S1 · The journal and the face
beats.text: Alice gets hold of Lucius Fox's coded journal, learns Kryptonite pierces the Batsuit, and delivers Tommy Elliot a promised new face — Bruce Wayne's.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The two weapons aimed at Batwoman at season's end. Both pay off immediately when the next season opens.

cliffhanger.text: Alice is loose in the sewers decoding Lucius Fox's journal for a way to kill Batwoman, and Tommy Elliot walks free wearing Bruce Wayne's face. Kate is holding the Kryptonite shard Supergirl entrusted to her.
questions: What will Alice do with a Kryptonite-tipped weapon and Bruce Wayne's own notes?
Who is Safiyah, the power Julia and the Rifle keep hinting at?
Can Kate stop Tommy Elliot from claiming Bruce's life along with his face?

characters.name: Kate Kane
characters.line: Bruce Wayne's cousin, out lesbian and Gotham's new Batwoman; has killed once and no longer believes her twin can be saved.

characters.name: Alice / Beth Kane
characters.line: Kate's twin, warped by years of captivity with the Cartwrights; on the run in the sewers and decoding a weapon against Batwoman.

characters.name: Jacob Kane
characters.line: Kate's father and head of the Crows private security firm; free after being framed, and has vowed to arrest Batwoman on sight.

characters.name: Mary Hamilton
characters.line: Kate's stepsister and unlicensed clinic doctor; has known Kate is Batwoman since her mother Catherine's death.

characters.name: Luke Fox
characters.line: Lucius Fox's son and Kate's tech partner in the Batcave; his father's murder cover-up was exposed and re-litigated this season.

characters.name: Sophie Moore
characters.line: Kate's ex and Crows agent; knows Kate is Batwoman and just kissed her under the Bat-Signal.

characters.name: Tommy Elliot / Hush
characters.line: Bruce Wayne's childhood friend and would-be killer, now surgically remade to wear Bruce's face.

beats.label: S2 · Ryan takes the suit
beats.text: Kate's plane crashes returning from National City; ex-con Ryan Wilder finds the Batsuit in the wreckage and uses it after being shot with the Kryptonite bullet.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The lead-actor handoff. Kate is gone, and Ryan — the person now under the cowl for the rest of the series — enters via the wound that shapes her whole season.

beats.label: S2 · Elliot returned
beats.text: Wearing Bruce's face, Tommy Elliot hunts Ryan for the Kryptonite bullet; she beats him back to Arkham, and Luke and Mary agree to let her keep the cowl.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes the S1 cliffhanger and formalises Ryan as Batwoman with the team's blessing.

beats.label: S2 · Coryana
beats.text: Safiyah, an island warlord, resurfaces as Alice's old rescuer; she reveals she erased Alice's memory of her lover Ocean and dangles Kate's survival as bait.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the season's antagonist axis and the false promise that Kate is alive out there — the lure that drives Alice's arc.

beats.label: S2 · Kryptonite poisoning
beats.text: Ryan's Kryptonite wound turns out to be fatal without the Desert Rose — the same plant whose blood cured Mary — pulling the team, Sophie and Jacob to Coryana.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The medical ticking clock that motivates the Coryana trip and forces the reveal that Kate never was on the island.

beats.label: S2 · Kate as Circe
beats.text: Crimelord Roman Sionis, the masked head of the False Face Society, has Kate captive; his hypnotist Enigma erases Kate's memory and remakes her face as his dead daughter Circe.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The reveal of where Kate actually is and why she doesn't come home yet. Reshapes the second half of the season into a rescue-then-restore arc.

beats.label: S2 · Kate hands off
beats.text: Alice and the Bat-team recover Kate as 'Circe'; Snakebite triggers a hallucination that lets Kate reassert, and she hands the cowl to Ryan and leaves Gotham to find Bruce.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The formal, in-story handoff. Ryan is Batwoman not by accident anymore; Kate is off the board.

beats.label: S2 · Crows disbanded, trophies loose
beats.text: Jacob disbands the corrupt Crows after Tavaroff shoots Luke; Alice is jailed, tells Ryan her birth mother lives, and Batman's stolen villain trophies scatter into the river.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Three separate launchpads into next season — no more Crows, a new personal mystery for Ryan, and the villain trophies that seed everything to come.

cliffhanger.text: Ryan is Gotham's Batwoman with Kate's blessing, but the Crows are gone and Batman's villain trophies — Poison Ivy's plants, Joker's acid-spraying flower, Mad Hatter's hat, Killer Croc's tooth and more — are drifting loose in a lawless city.
questions: Whose hands will Batman's scattered villain trophies fall into?
Who is the biological mother Alice claims is alive, and why is she telling Ryan now?
Without the Crows, who actually polices Gotham as the trophies surface?

characters.name: Ryan Wilder
characters.line: A formerly homeless ex-con who found the Batsuit in Kate's plane wreck; publicly Batwoman with Kate's blessing.

characters.name: Kate Kane
characters.line: Recovered from her captivity and disfigurement; has left Gotham to search for the missing Bruce.

characters.name: Alice / Beth
characters.line: Publicly exposed as Beth Kane and imprisoned at Arkham after helping bring Kate back.

characters.name: Mary Hamilton
characters.line: Full member of the Bat-team; her healing Desert Rose blood is now a widely-known asset.

characters.name: Luke Fox
characters.line: Shot by a corrupt Crow and recovering; runs the Batcave and has taken up his father's secretly-built Batsuit as Batwing.

characters.name: Sophie Moore
characters.line: Quit the Crows over their racist corruption; now firmly on Ryan's side and knows she is Batwoman.

characters.name: Jacob Kane
characters.line: Disbanded his own Crows after their crimes came to light; reunited briefly with his daughter Beth before her arrest.

beats.label: S3 · Trophy hunt
beats.text: GCPD's new Detective Renee Montoya learns Batwoman's identity and forces her to hunt down the loose Batman-villain trophies — partnered with Alice, on furlough from Arkham.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's whole engine: the coerced Ryan-Alice partnership, and the trophy list that turns out to be a cover for Renee's real mission.

beats.label: S3 · Ryan's family
beats.text: Ryan discovers Jeturian CEO Jada Jet is her birth mother; charming half-brother Marquis welcomes her, hiding that a childhood shock from Joker's buzzer made him a sociopath.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Answers the S2 cliffhanger and plants Marquis, whose Joker-buzzer damage is the ticking bomb the second half of the season resolves.

beats.label: S3 · Mary infected
beats.text: While investigating a botanical Batman-villain trophy, Mary is dragged off by a vine and slowly infected with Poison Ivy's pheromones, drifting from Ryan toward Alice.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts the plot trigger for Poison Mary in place and starts Mary's shift toward Alice, which reshapes every team dynamic afterward.

beats.label: S3 · Marquis takes Wayne
beats.text: Ryan agrees to freeze Marquis in exchange for a Mary cure; Marquis escapes to seize Wayne Enterprises, and Mary destroys the cure herself, embracing her Poison Mary identity.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Two enemies at once — Marquis is now the CEO and Mary is committed to Ivy — and the cure that would fix either is gone.

beats.label: S3 · Ivy freed
beats.text: The Bat-team realises Renee's whole trophy hunt was cover to free Poison Ivy, whom Batman had hidden dying deep in the Batcave; Renee spirits her out and Mary defects to Ivy's cause.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The retroactive explanation for the entire season's premise. Reframes Renee and locks in the Ivy-Mary alliance as the final threat.

beats.label: S3 · Sanity restored
beats.text: Mary rejects Ivy in time to help Batwoman foil her plan to break Gotham's dam; Renee flees with Ivy for Coryana, and the joy-buzzer is repaired and used to restore Marquis's sanity.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Resolves both villain arcs — Mary is back, Marquis is fixed — and clears the deck for whatever the final scene is teeing up.

beats.label: S3 · A skeletal figure
beats.text: Alice, mind unravelling, is sent to an overseas sanitarium with Mary's blessing; a mangled, skeletal figure then attacks reporter Dana DeWitt at the crashed Batblimp's remains.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The single unresolved thread the show ended on. Whatever comes next, this is the image the returning viewer needs to be holding.

cliffhanger.text: The Bat-team have retaken Wayne Enterprises and reunited as a family, but a hazmat-suited news crew is attacked at the Batblimp crash site by a mangled, skeletal figure no one has identified. Alice is now oceans away, and Poison Ivy has escaped Gotham with Renee.
questions: Who — or what — is the skeletal figure at the Batblimp site?
Can an overseas sanitarium actually reach Alice, or is Beth Kane finally lost for good?
With Ivy loose on Coryana and Renee gone, who fills the vacuum on both sides?

characters.name: Ryan Wilder
characters.line: Gotham's Batwoman and reinstated CEO of Wayne Enterprises; now formally in her birth family's life.

characters.name: Alice / Beth
characters.line: Mentally unravelling and hallucinating; just committed to an overseas sanitarium with Mary's blessing.

characters.name: Mary Hamilton
characters.line: Restored from her Poison Mary persona; was Alice's personal physician at Arkham before signing off on her transfer overseas.

characters.name: Luke Fox
characters.line: Fully accepted the Batwing mantle after the Lucius A.I. sacrificed itself to redirect the Batblimp.

characters.name: Sophie Moore
characters.line: Ryan's girlfriend; worked the trophy hunt from the Batcave alongside Renee before her defection.

characters.name: Jada Jet
characters.line: Ryan's estranged birth mother and Jeturian Industries CEO; now formally in Ryan's life after Marquis's cure.

characters.name: Marquis Jet
characters.line: Ryan's half-brother, sanity restored by Joker's repaired buzzer; back at Jada's side, no longer a threat.

characters.name: Renee Montoya
characters.line: GCPD detective whose loose-trophies mission was a ruse to save her old lover Poison Ivy; has fled with her toward Coryana.
